old_title: Acts done by several persons in furtherance of common intention
new_title: General Explanations - Joint Liability & Common Intention
statutory_changes: Moved into general principles section under Section 3(5) BNS.
landmark_judgments: Barendra Kumar Ghosh v. Emperor (1925) 52 IA 40
Pandurang v. State of Hyderabad (1955) 1 SCR 1083

new_title: Criminal conspiracy punishment
statutory_changes: Consolidated under Chapter IV of BNS; defines agreement to do an illegal act.
landmark_judgments: State (NCT of Delhi) v. Navjot Sandhu (2005) 11 SCC 600
Kehar Singh v. State (Delhi Admn.) (1988) 3 SCC 609

new_title: Act endangering sovereignty, unity and integrity of India
statutory_changes: Word 'sedition' removed; replaced with acts endangering sovereignty, secession, or subversive activities.
landmark_judgments: Kedar Nath Singh v. State of Bihar (1962) Supp (2) SCR 769
S.G. Vombatkere v. Union of India (2022) 7 SCC 633

new_title: Punishment for murder
statutory_changes: Section 103(1) re-enacts Section 302 IPC. Section 103(2) introduces separate punishment for mob lynching.
landmark_judgments: Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab (1980) 2 SCC 684
Machhi Singh v. State of Punjab (1983) 3 SCC 470

new_title: Causing death by negligence
statutory_changes: Rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide. Section 106(2) hit-and-run held in abeyance.
landmark_judgments: Syed Akbar v. State of Karnataka (1980) 1 SCC 30
Jacob Mathew v. State of Punjab (2005) 6 SCC 1

new_title: Attempt to murder
statutory_changes: Substantive elements preserved. Re-numbered under BNS Chapter VI.
landmark_judgments: State of Maharashtra v. Balram Bama Patil (1983) 2 SCC 28
Hari Singh v. State of Haryana (2002) 2 SCC 335

new_title: Rape defined
statutory_changes: Seven statutory consent circumstances retained; re-numbered under Chapter V (Offences against Women and Children).
landmark_judgments: Tukaram v. State of Maharashtra (1979) 2 SCC 143
Independent Thought v. Union of India (2017) 10 SCC 800

new_title: Theft punishment and community service
statutory_changes: Theft defined in 303(1). 303(2) provides up to 3 years imprisonment or fine or community service for petty theft.
landmark_judgments: K.N. Mehra v. State of Rajasthan (1957) SCR 623

new_title: Criminal breach of trust defined
statutory_changes: Core ingredients of entrustment and dishonest misappropriation preserved. Punishment under 316(2) up to 5 years.
landmark_judgments: Chelloor Mankkal Narayan Ittirishi Nambudiri v. State of Travancore-Cochin (1952) SCR 219
Jaswantrai Manilal Akhaney v. State of Bombay (1956) SCR 483

old_title: Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property
new_title: Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property
statutory_changes: Cheating consolidated under Section 318. Sub-section (4) corresponds directly to old Section 420 IPC.
landmark_judgments: Hridaya Ranjan Prasad Verma v. State of Bihar (2000) 4 SCC 168
Vesa Holdings (P) Ltd. v. State of Kerala (2015) 8 SCC 293

old_title: Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty
new_title: Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty
statutory_changes: Cruelty defined identically; moved into Chapter V (Offences against Women and Children).
landmark_judgments: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar (2014) 8 SCC 273
Preeti Gupta v. State of Jharkhand (2010) 7 SCC 667

old_title: When police may arrest without warrant
new_title: When police may arrest without warrant & safeguards
statutory_changes: Adds mandatory DSP prior permission before arresting infirm or elderly accused for offenses under 3 years.
landmark_judgments: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar (2014) 8 SCC 273
D.K. Basu v. State of West Bengal (1997) 1 SCC 416

new_title: Information in cognizable cases & Electronic FIR
statutory_changes: Formally introduces e-FIR (must be signed within 3 days). Provides preliminary inquiry up to 14 days for offences punishable 3 to 7 years.
landmark_judgments: Lalita Kumari v. Govt. of U.P. (2014) 2 SCC 1
State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335

new_title: Magistrate power to order investigation with affidavit precondition
statutory_changes: Codifies Priyanka Srivastava mandate: citizen must attach affidavit verifying Section 173(4) SP exhaustion.
landmark_judgments: Priyanka Srivastava v. State of U.P. (2015) 6 SCC 287
Sakiri Vasu v. State of U.P. (2008) 2 SCC 409

old_title: Procedure when investigation cannot be completed in 24 hours
new_title: Custody remand and default bail timeline
statutory_changes: Allows 15 days police custody in whole or in parts during initial 40 or 60 days of judicial remand.
landmark_judgments: CBI v. Anupam J. Kulkarni (1992) 3 SCC 141
V. Senthil Balaji v. State (2023) 10 SCC 409

old_title: Direction for grant of bail to person apprehending arrest (Anticipatory Bail)
new_title: Direction for grant of bail to person apprehending arrest
statutory_changes: Preserves Session Court and High Court concurrent anticipatory bail jurisdiction.
landmark_judgments: Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia v. State of Punjab (1980) 2 SCC 565
Sushila Aggarwal v. State (NCT of Delhi) (2020) 5 SCC 1

old_title: Saving of inherent powers of High Court
new_title: Saving of inherent powers of High Court
statutory_changes: Verbatim reproduction of High Court inherent powers to quash proceedings to prevent abuse of process.
landmark_judgments: State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335
R.P. Kapur v. State of Punjab (1960) 3 SCR 388

new_title: Definitions: Document includes Electronic & Digital Records
statutory_changes: Digital records, emails, messages, and cloud files elevated directly into primary definition of document.
landmark_judgments: Arjun Panditrao Khotkar v. Kailash Kushanrao Gorantyal (2020) 7 SCC 1

new_title: Admissibility of electronic records and certificate requirement
statutory_changes: Retains mandatory certificate requirement for secondary electronic evidence with modern server parameters.
landmark_judgments: Anvar P.V. v. P.K. Basheer (2014) 10 SCC 473
Arjun Panditrao Khotkar v. Kailash Kushanrao Gorantyal (2020) 7 SCC 1

old_title: Presumption as to absence of consent in certain prosecutions for rape
new_title: Presumption as to absence of consent in certain prosecutions for rape
statutory_changes: Preserves statutory presumption where sexual intercourse is proved and woman states in evidence she did not consent.
landmark_judgments: State of Punjab v. Gurmit Singh (1996) 2 SCC 382
